title: Tuckman: team-development stages
rows: Inclusion; quiet, polite, guarded, impersonal and businesslike behavior; initially high morale. Transition toward testing is marked at the edge of this stage.
Infighting, conflict over control, confrontation, alienation, personal agendas and low morale.
Becoming organized: establish procedures, develop team skills, confront issues and rebuild morale.
Productivity, trust, flexibility, support, confidence, efficiency and high morale.
The original diagram shows a convening-to-adjourning cycle.
note: Rebuilt from the source diagram. These are model descriptions, not inevitable behaviors or a diagnostic measure.

title: Punctuated equilibrium: change can occur in bursts
rows: First meeting: a relatively stable initial working pattern
Midpoint transition: a marked change in approach
Later work: additional advances toward completion
note: The original step-shaped performance curve uses a midpoint and deadline. No numerical performance scale or universal timing is established.

title: Serial network: every activity follows the previous one
note: Edges: A → B → C → D → E → F → G → H. No durations are supplied. This is the paper-and-presentation example, not the numerical survey table.

title: Parallel network: split the work and merge at completion
rows: A Identify topic → B Research → C Paper draft
C → D Edit paper → F Final draft → H Finish
C → E Prepare presentation → G Finish presentation → H Finish
Both F and G must finish before H.
note: Reconstructs all source activities and edges: A→B, B→C, C→D, C→E, D→F, E→G, F→H, G→H. There are no durations or resource allocations.

title: Uncertainty and the amount at stake
rows: Opportunity and uncertainty are higher; committed stake is lower.
Amount at stake rises as work and commitments accumulate.
